leads.reason: Near-duplicate of ott_013 (register objectid 143), a golden weeping willow roughly 300m south along the same Queen Elizabeth Driveway pathway. This one's NCC description is a generic species blurb with no planting date or distinguishing detail ('an ideal ornamental species for areas near ponds, lakes...'), unlike ott_013's dated, specimen-specific description. Shipping both this close together, of the same species with one having nothing to say for itself, would read as padding. Worth reconsidering only if a distinguishing fact turns up for this specific tree.

Location confirmed via reverse geocoding as the Rideau River Eastern Pathway, New Edinburgh/Rockcliffe Park border, Ottawa (genuinely in Ottawa, unlike the Jacques-Cartier Park entries below). But the NCC register description is entirely generic ('a hardy species... planted extensively in North America... able to reproduce in the wild'), naming no age, size or specific history for this individual tree, so it does not argue for itself as worth the walk. Note for whoever picks this up: Rockcliffe Park does have a well-documented 'grove of Black Locust trees' embellished with a stone circle by Carver, Hazeland and Graham as part of a 1967 Centennial Village Green project (rockcliffepark.ca/environment-and-outdoor-spaces), but that feature sits near Springfield Road and Mariposa Avenue, a different location within the historic district from this tree's coordinate on the Rideau River pathway. Do not bridge that story onto this specimen without confirming they are the same trees; it looks like they are not.

Register describes this as standing in Jacques-Cartier Park, which reverse geocoding confirms is in Hull, Gatineau, Quebec, not Ottawa, Ontario. Out of scope for the Ottawa city file; would need a Gatineau city file if/when one exists. Do not publish under Ottawa.

2026-09-16 verify pass. Register (NCC 'A Living Legacy') description is strong on narrative ('This magnificent Douglas-fir in Commissioners Park serves as an introduction to the Ottawa lumber tycoon John Rudolphus Booth, who took advantage of the depression of 1874-1876 to buy forest concessions at a discount') and Commissioners Park's own history as Booth's former lumberyard is independently confirmed (Wikipedia, 'Commissioners Park (Ottawa)'), but that confirms the PARK's history, not this specific tree: no second source was found naming or dating this individual specimen. Checked iNaturalist for Pseudotsuga menziesii/Pseudotsuga at 100m, 300m and 500m radius: zero matching observations within 100-300m, one casual-grade Pseudotsuga menziesii var. glauca observation (id 114935111, 2022) roughly 500m away, too far and the wrong variety to be this tree. Two WebSearch attempts (Commissioners Park Douglas fir Booth; Commissioners Park Douglas-fir conifer tour) found nothing further. One source only; does not clear the two-independent-sources bar. Worth reconsidering if a Commissioners Park tree walk, tulip-festival press piece or NCC blog post naming this conifer turns up.

leads.species: Cypress Oak / English fastigiate oak (Quercus robur f. fastigiata)
leads.reason: 2026-09-16 verify pass. Register (NCC 'A Living Legacy') description: 'This Queen Elizabeth Driveway Cyprus oak and the surrounding and accompanying trees in this area were planted in all likelihood in the mid-1950s, around the time when the Dominion Arboretum began growing this variety' (note the register's own hedge, 'in all likelihood', which is itself a vague-source estimate rather than a documented date). No second source found: iNaturalist has zero Quercus/Quercus robur observations within 150m of the coordinate, and a WebSearch for the cultivar on Queen Elizabeth Driveway/Dominion Arboretum returned only generic background on what a 'cypress oak' cultivar is, nothing about this planting. One source only; does not clear the two-independent-sources bar. Distinct from ott_002/ott_003 (Tilia platyphyllos 'Vitifolia', a different QED avenue tree already published) and not a duplicate of anything live.
